title: Cofinal κ-directed poset replacement for a small filtered quasicategory
statement:
Use universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, $\kappa$-small simplicial sets and $\kappa$-filtered quasicategories from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and nerves, coherent functors and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory. There exist a $\mathcal U$-small partially ordered set $A$ and a coherent functor $u:N(A)\to I$ with the following properties. Every subset of $A$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has an upper bound, including the empty subset, so $A$ is nonempty. The functor $u$ is cofinal: for every coherent diagram $F:I\to\mathcal C$ in a quasicategory $\mathcal C$ admitting small colimits, restriction of a colimiting cocone along $u$ is colimiting. Equivalently the induced comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_{a\in N(A)}F(u(a))\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F(i)$$
is an equivalence, natural in $F$ and respecting the restricted cocone legs.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384, with cofinality in its colimit-invariance meaning (Proposition 4.1.1.8) Online text read 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/ (WANTED). No Stacks tag supplies this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Take a small set $X$ of cardinality $\kappa$ and choose $x_0\in X$, possible because $\kappa$ is infinite. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pair-groupoid-thickening] to $I,X,x_0$. Thus $E_X$ has exactly one arrow between each ordered pair, $K=I\times N(E_X)$ is a small quasicategory, and the projection $p:K\to I$ is a coherent functor equivalence with the specified constant-coordinate section $s$. We retain the vertex-sequence description $(N(E_X))_n=X^{n+1}$ for the fresh-coordinate cone construction below.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text:
For every quasicategory $\mathcal C$ in a sufficiently large universe, the equivalence $p$ of step 1 is a Joyal weak equivalence by clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations]. Apply [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii): the actual precomposition map $p^*:\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is a coherent functor equivalence. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it therefore induces equivalences on all mapping spaces, in particular
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal C)}(F,\Delta_Iy)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(Fp,\Delta_Ky),$$
where $p^*\Delta_Iy=\Delta_Ky$ strictly.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text:
Let $\lambda:F\to\Delta_IL$ be a colimiting cocone on $F:I\to\mathcal C$. The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies its universal-property map at $y$ as an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal C)}(F,\Delta_Iy).$$
The universal-property map of $p^*\lambda$ is its composite with the mapping-space equivalence of step 2: precomposition sends $\lambda$ to $p^*\lambda$, constant transformations to the same constant transformations, and their composite to their composite. Thus it too is an equivalence for every $y$. The same cocone criterion makes $p^*\lambda$ colimiting. Its apex is still $L$ and its legs are exactly the restrictions along $p$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text: Let $L\subseteq K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial subset, including $L=\varnothing$. The projection $L\to I$ has a coherent cocone by $\kappa$-filteredness. Apply the opposite dual of the fixed-boundary join comparison [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to realize it as a simplicial extension $f:L^{\triangleright}\to I$ of this exact map $L\to I$. Choose $x\in X$ outside the second coordinates of the vertices of $L$; this is possible since there are fewer than $\kappa$ vertices. There is a unique extension $g:L^{\triangleright}\to N(E_X)$ of the second projection which sends the cone point to $x$: a simplex in this nerve is determined by its vertex sequence. Put $h=(f,g)$. This extends the inclusion $L\hookrightarrow K$ and is injective in every degree. To check injectivity, the positions having second coordinate $x$ in a coned simplex are precisely its final cone positions, since no vertex of the base has coordinate $x$. They determine the splitting into base and cone; restriction to the base recovers its simplex because $h|_L$ is the inclusion. Pure cone simplices are distinguished from base simplices in the same way. Thus its image $L'=h(L^{\triangleright})$ is isomorphic to the right cone, with specified apex. Its nondegenerate simplices consist of those of $L$, one cone on each of them, and the apex, so their number is $2|L_{\mathrm{nd}}|+1<\kappa$. For $\kappa=\aleph_0$ this is a finite number.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text: Let $A$ be the set of all $\kappa$-small simplicial subsets $K_a\subseteq K$ which admit a right-cone presentation, ordered by inclusion; choose one presentation and apex $t_a$ for each. This is a small partially ordered set, since it is a subcollection of the power set of the small set of simplices of $K$. Given fewer than $\kappa$ elements of $A$, their union $L$ is a simplicial subset with fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices. Each nondegenerate simplex of the union belongs to a constituent and is nondegenerate there; regularity of $\kappa$ bounds the union of these fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$. Apply step 4 to $L$ to obtain a cone subset containing them all, an upper bound in $A$. The same argument with the empty union gives an element of $A$. Finally every simplex of $K$ lies in a finite simplicial subset generated by that simplex, whose nondegenerate simplices are among its finitely many faces. Step 4 places that subset in a member of $A$, proving $K=\bigcup_a K_a$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text: The small nonempty poset $A$, the increasing cover $K=\bigcup_a K_a$ and the chosen right-cone presentations satisfy [lem-coef-infinity-directed-cone-cover]; in particular finite subsets of $A$ have upper bounds by step 5. Obtain the coherent cofinal map $j:N(A)\to K$ with vertices $t_a$. Define $u=pj:N(A)\to I$. Given $F:I\to\mathcal C$ and a colimiting cocone, step 3 makes its restriction along $p$ colimiting, and the cone-cover lemma makes the further restriction along $j$ colimiting. This is exactly restriction along $u$, with the original vertex and legs. The unique colimit comparison is therefore an equivalence. Its naturality follows from the universal property: composing the restricted cocone with a transformation $F\to F'$ gives the same cocone maps in either order. The upper-bound assertion for subsets of size less than $\kappa$, including the empty subset, is step 5.
